cohort: The study included 1,507 women with term singleton pregnancies, prolonged rupture of membranes (>=18 h), and unknown Group B Streptococcus colonization status.
finding: Among women with unknown GBS status and prolonged ROM, the prophylactic use of clindamycin compared to ampicillin was associated with higher rates of maternal infectious morbidity and adverse neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Clindamycin treatment was associated with a higher rate of cesarean delivery (36.0% vs. 18.1%) compared to ampicillin.
